edits.after: 2.1 For one morphism between quasi-projective varieties, choose a locally closed embedding of its source into $\mathbb P^N$ and take the reduced closure of its graph in $\mathbb P^N\times Y$. The graph is locally closed, hence open in that closure; thus the map factors as an open inclusion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ followed by the projective projection $p:\overline X\to Y$. The closure is quasi-projective and $p$ is analytically proper by [F1]. Choose [F1]'s one-map Whitney strata for $p$, respecting the boundary $\overline X\setminus X$ and the finite input supports. Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact; $Rj_*$ is locally computed by the ordinary sections on the open part of [F2]'s controlled link-cone chart, and [F3] and [F4] give the bounded finite, locally constant complex-stratum model and its actual restriction maps. The proper whole-fibre local trivializations of [F2] give, over a small ball in each target stratum, a product with a compact stratified fibre. The same derived product reconstruction used in [F3] identifies the constructible input there with a fibre object constant in the ball direction, so its pushforward is its finite fibre cochain complex constant along that ball. Finitely many target strata give a uniform amplitude bound; the actual restriction and support comparisons show $Rp_*Rj_*$ and $Rp_*j_!$ compute $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ respectively. All models and comparisons commute with field extension by [F3] and [F4]. For a general separated finite-type map, work over an affine target chart, take a finite affine cover of its source preimage and finite intersections, and apply this construction to their finite disjoint union mapping to the target. Prescribe the needed supports in that one-map construction, obtaining one target stratification for the finitely many terms. The actual finite open-cover derived augmentation of [F5] then assembles ordinary pushforward; its extension-by-zero support resolution assembles proper-support pushforward. Thus the outputs are bounded algebraically constructible locally on the target and hence globally by a finite affine cover. This proof uses a constructed projective factorization on each quasi-projective piece and proper whole-fibre triviality, rather than inferring whole-fibre control from local source charts. No joint stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram is required. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎
